title: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman identifies his teachers as Rav Chisda and Rav Sheshet, as we find in Shabbat 54b: He sat before Rav Chisda, and he sat and said — Rav Nachman said to him, 'If so, you have made him Yalta.' (Hyman records Rashal’s reading as: he sat before Rav Nachman.)
Hyman cites Pesachim 46a for an instance in which Rav Pappa bar Shmuel resolves a difficulty raised by Rav Chisda.
And in Ketubot 37a: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel said in the name of Rav Sheshet. And there, 36b: he raised an objection against Rav Yosef.

And, as Hyman infers, when Abaye and Rava were before Rabbah and Rav Yosef, Rav Pappa bar Shmuel was then one of the judges of Pumbedita, as in Sanhedrin 17b: 'They said: the judges of Pumbedita' — Rav Pappa bar Shmuel.

And in Rosh Hashanah 27a: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel thought to act in accordance with the mishnah; Rava said to him, etc. And there, 34b: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel rose to pray; Rava said to him: They did not say, etc.
And in Sanhedrin 26b: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel thought to declare it valid — Rava said to him, etc.

And in Bava Kamma 84a: a case in which a certain [one] cut off a child's hand came before Rav Pappa bar Shmuel, who said to him — Rava said to him: But we learned in a mishnah — he [Rav Pappa bar Shmuel] said to him — Abaye said to him, etc. And Hyman relates in Bava Metzia 60b: a certain old slave who had dyed his beard came to Rava so that he would buy him, but he did not want to; he came to Rav Pappa bar Shmuel and he bought him. One day he said to the slave, 'Give me water to drink'; he went and washed the dye from his beard and said to him, 'See that I am older than your father.' He read of himself: 'The righteous is delivered from trouble' (this is Rava) 'and another comes in his place.'

And in Bava Batra 90b: he instituted [supplied שתיקו] a kayla of three kefizei, and sent to Pumbedita (in Hyman’s explanation, he wanted the people of his city to accept it as a measure), but they did not agree, and he sent to Papunai, and they accepted it, and it was called 'Roz Pappa.' And there, 73b, concerning the stories of Rabbah bar bar Chana [רבב״ח], Rav Pappa bar Shmuel said: If I had not been there, I would not have believed it.

notes.text: Hyman's citation abbreviates the speaker as ר״נ, conventionally read as Nachman; the title is left abbreviated here. The parenthetical records Rashal's reading, according to which he sat before ר״נ rather than before Rav Chisda.
עשיתיו ילתא is rendered literally ('you have made him Yalta'); Hyman does not explain the sense of the remark.
Hyman presents this dating as his own inference ('as it appears', כפי הנראה); the Sanhedrin passage is cited as naming him among the judges of Pumbedita.
Folio references follow Hyman's printed labels: a colon marks side b of the folio and a period marks side a.

כיילא בת ג׳ קפיזי (a kayla measure of three kefizei) and רוז פפא are given in transliteration; פאפונאי is a place name as printed. The printed שתיקו is translated 'he instituted', presumably for שתיקן. דרבב״ח is the standard abbreviation for Rabbah bar bar Chana.
The term 'ילתא' is rendered 'Yalta' as a name; Hyman's wording 'עשיתיו ילתא' is preserved literally without further explanation.

The consulted Shabbat 54b has Rav Pappa sitting before Rav Chisda, with Rav Nachman making the Yalta remark about the animal. The consulted Vilna Chokhmat Shlomo on that passage specifically gives ‘before Rav Nachman’ as the alternative reading, agreeing with Hyman’s report of Rashal. Hyman’s masculine wording is translated literally. Ketubot 36b–37a names Rav Pappa bar Shmuel in the exchange with Rav Yosef and gives the answer in Rav Sheshet’s name. The Sanhedrin 17b list identifies Rav Pappa bar Shmuel by the phrase ‘judges of Pumbedita.’ Hyman’s reconstruction of when he held that role remains an inference.

At the cited Pesachim 46a the consulted text gives Rav Pappa, without a patronymic, objecting to Rava’s treatment of the kneading bowl. The consulted 46b exchange instead has Rabbah asking Rav Chisda about baking from a festival for Shabbat. The precise Rav Chisda exchange Hyman attributes to Rav Pappa bar Shmuel remains unverified.

Hyman’s printed Bava Kamma 84a excerpt (vol. III, p. 1029) omits the subject’s noun and abbreviates the speeches. In the full cited passage, a donkey cuts off a child’s hand, Rav Pappa speaks, Rava objects, Rav Pappa replies and Abaye objects. The translation keeps the supplied excerpt’s gaps. The same printed page reads שתיקן (‘instituted’) in the Bava Batra 90b measure story, alongside supplied שתיקו and the consulted Gemara’s תקין. The Gemara says they called the three-kefizei measure Roz Pappa.
